tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.take: Tulane arrives reeling after six turnovers in a blowout home loss to UTSA, while Charlotte just snapped a 16-game losing streak against FBS competition with a stunner at Temple behind Conner Harrell's four touchdowns. The history still leans one way — Tulane has outscored Charlotte 61-3 across the last two meetings — and the market has already cut this number from around -13.5 toward -8.5. No true edge at the current prices: the best Tulane number is a touch worse than fair, but the lean is Tulane because the Green Wave's run game and defense are the steadier units against a Charlotte offense that just played its best game of the season.
games.title: Tulane @ Charlotte
games.verdict: LEAN: Tulane — no true edge, but the lean is Tulane because the run game and defense are steadier than a Charlotte side coming off one big night.

games.take: The Space Game, and both teams arrive 4-3 with very different weeks behind them: UCF is six days removed from a double-overtime win over No. 2 BYU, while Baylor is playing its first game since Dave Aranda's dismissal, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman as interim head coach. UCF leans on Keyone Jenkins and a heavy inside-zone run game; Baylor's DJ Lagway finally looked comfortable running the ball at Kansas. No true edge at the current prices — the best number on either side is still worse than fair — but the lean is UCF because the home side has the steadier situation, the fresher big win, and a run game built for a Friday night in the Bounce House.
games.title: Baylor @ UCF
games.verdict: LEAN: UCF — no true edge, but the lean is UCF because the home side's situation is steadier than an interim-coach Baylor team on its second straight loss.

games.matchup: Kent State Golden Flashes @ Sacramento State Hornets
games.take: This one is on the board, and the edge is on the spread, not the moneyline: Sacramento State +7.5 at even money beats a 51.4% devigged Pinnacle fair for +2.9% EV, while the rest of the market hangs -108 to -118 on the same number. Kent State (3-5) needs wins to stay alive for bowl eligibility, but the Flashes travel 2,400 miles for a 7:30 PM PT kick — their third road game in four weeks — and the line has already been cut from around -11 to -7.5. The lean is Sacramento State plus the points because the number moved toward the home dog and the travel spot is real.
games.title: Kent State @ Sacramento State
games.verdict: LEAN: Sacramento State +7.5 — a real edge on the spread, because the line has been cut from around -11 and Kent State is on a cross-country late kick.

games.take: An NBA Cup rematch four days after Charlotte's 110-103 win in the first meeting. This one is on the board: Charlotte +104 beats a 49.8% devigged Pinnacle fair for +1.5% EV while the rest of the market sits at -102 to +102. The honest counterweight is real — Charlotte is without Coby White, Kon Knueppel and Grant Williams, Dennis Schroder is questionable, and Washington gets No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa back for his home debut. The lean is Charlotte anyway because the price, not the matchup, is the edge: Pinnacle says this is a coin flip, and one book is still paying plus money.
games.title: Hornets @ Wizards
games.verdict: LEAN: Charlotte +104 — a real edge, because Pinnacle calls this a coin flip and one book is still paying plus money.

games.take: NBA Cup group play: 4-1 Detroit at 0-4 Brooklyn. The Pistons are doing this without Jalen Duren (hamstring, out at least two weeks), with Paul Reed stepping in at center, while Brooklyn is still looking for its first win behind one of the league's leakiest defenses. Detroit's moneyline is overpriced everywhere — the best number is -317 against a 74.5% fair — while Brooklyn +290 is essentially right on the fair number. No true edge either way, but the lean is Brooklyn plus the points on price: the dog's number is the honest one, and Detroit is on its fourth game in six nights.
games.title: Pistons @ Nets
games.verdict: LEAN: Brooklyn — no true edge, but the lean is Brooklyn because +290 is essentially the fair number while Detroit's price is overcooked.

games.take: Houston is the better team and the market knows it — the only question is whether the price pays you for it. The best US number on Houston is -215, worth about +0.5% against the 68.6% devigged Pinnacle fair: close to the bar, not over it. Dallas at +200 is worse than fair. No true edge at a US book, but the lean is Houston because the Rockets are the right side of a fair number that still gives them nearly seven chances in ten, and the Dallas price offers nothing back.
games.title: Rockets @ Mavericks
games.verdict: LEAN: Houston — no true edge at a US book, but the lean is Houston because the fair number still gives the Rockets nearly seven chances in ten.

games.matchup: Los Angeles Lakers @ Golden State Warriors
games.take: The nightcap, and a good example of why the lean follows the price and not the jersey. The Lakers are the fair favorite at 57.2%, but the best Lakers number is -144 — worse than fair — while Golden State +127 is the closer of the two prices to its 42.8% fair share. No true edge on either side. The lean is Golden State as a home dog because its price is the honest one; laying -144 on a road favorite the market already prices at -140 is paying full freight.
games.title: Lakers @ Warriors
games.verdict: LEAN: Golden State — no true edge, but the lean is Golden State because +127 is closer to the fair number than laying -144 on the Lakers.
